anchor: 100 emails over three weeks: 15 people replied, closed 2 deals.
reported: 100 emails, 15 replies, two deals, three weeks.
calculation: 15/100 = 15% total replies; 2/100 = 2% sends-to-deals. If both deals came from those replies, 2/15 = 13.33% reply-to-deal.
limits: Single small cohort; unclear unique-recipient denominator, positive replies, deal value, collection, attribution and contact resolution. Does not establish causality or a Mindmaxing forecast.

anchor: Cost: my weekend plus $0.30 in API calls
reported: $0.30 API calls plus a weekend of work; earlier subscriptions quoted at $300–$400/month.
calculation: No valid fully loaded CAC calculation is possible.
limits: Lead list already existed; labor, inboxes, sourcing, data access and maintenance are excluded or unclear.

reported: 3–5% baseline replies for ordinary outbound with a reasonable list.
calculation: None; no cohort provided.
limits: Total versus interested replies is not specified. Same author gives different thresholds in T20; not independent studies.

anchor: Exposures (DMs) - 350 Conversations - 35 Clients - 7 Price - £1500
reported: 350 exposures → 35 conversations → seven clients × £1,500 = £10,500.
calculation: 10% exposure-to-conversation; 20% conversation-to-close; 2% exposure-to-close.
limits: Explicit example with assumed values, not measured performance. One reply incorrectly challenges it as a 10% close rate.

anchor: get 7 domains, 3 inboxes each
reported: Seven domains × three inboxes; 300 daily sends; two-week warmup; later ramp from five to 20 cold sends/inbox/day.
calculation: 21 inboxes × 20 sends = 420/day at the later stated cap, not the initial 300/day.
limits: Not a verified provider policy, safe limit or minimum viable experiment size. Automated warmup and a sub-3% bounce target require current independent validation before implementation.

anchor: Last month I got 3 clients from Reddit, 2 from Linkedin, 1 from Twitter, and 4 from Cold emailing.
reported: Three Reddit, two LinkedIn, one Twitter, four cold-email clients in the prior month; then an example ten × $2k AOV.
calculation: Channel counts sum to ten; ten × $2,000 = $20,000 only at the assumed AOV.
limits: No denominator, channel costs, attribution method or evidence that every reported client actually paid $2k.

anchor: These two clients referred me the next 5
reported: Two initial introductions; next five referred clients; a deeper connector helped with another 15; connectors were paid.
calculation: No conversion rate or commission percentage available.
limits: Narrative chain, not a time-bounded audited cohort; do not extrapolate predictable introductions per client.

anchor: We're at consistent €8k weeks now and l've sent over 4 million cold emails
reported: €8k weeks; four million-plus cold emails across multiple clients.
calculation: No margin, monthly recurring revenue or campaign conversion calculation supported.
limits: Self-report challenged in comments; volume spans unspecified time and clients. Do not describe as verified revenue or personal outreach by one campaign.

anchor: I keep every sequence at max 2 emails
reported: Under 80 words; maximum two emails; new angle after 30–45 days; judge over three to four weeks; one channel for 60 days.
calculation: None.
limits: Conflicts with T19. New-angle contact must not bypass an opt-out or other suppression condition.

anchor: Separate sending domains, 5 inboxes per domain, 30 emails max per inbox
reported: Separate domains, five inboxes/domain, 30 emails/inbox/day, two-week minimum warmup.
calculation: 150 sends/domain/day under that proposal.
limits: Historical advice, not verified current technical limits or immunity from reputation problems. No sending configuration is adopted by this index.

anchor: With linkedin you'll add another 10% replies from the list.
reported: Another 10% replies after adding LinkedIn.
calculation: Cannot distinguish a relative lift from ten percentage points.
limits: No sample, baseline, control or attribution; financial/product interest disclosed.

anchor: 448 outreaches, 33 responses, 21 Looms, 5 calls.
reported: 448 outreaches → 33 responses → 21 Looms → five calls; OP says two sales-call prospects have budget/timing constraints.
calculation: Reply 7.37%; calls/outreach 1.12%; calls/responses 15.15%. Looms/responses 63.64% if the stages are nested.
limits: The screenshot-derived post table omits values. Looms may be sent rather than watched. Closed-sale count unavailable; do not assign zero or forecast 1–2 wins from five calls.

anchor: maybe 300 so far and no ones interested
reported: Roughly 300 attempts; weekly 120 WhatsApps plus 120 calls to the same people, little interest.
calculation: No precise unique-prospect conversion rate supported.
limits: Repeated touches, vague outcome language and no complete counts. Valuable counterexample to automatic success from branded mockups.

anchor: they run campaigns for me, and got 35% of order value.
reported: 35% of order value to a lead-generation agency; claimed average ticket $1,000 and target of at least five new clients/month.
calculation: At a $1,000 order, 35% is $350 before fulfilment and other costs.
limits: Target client volume is not confirmed achieved volume. Not the commission to adopt for Mindmaxing brokers.

anchor: I am sending nearly 100k emails monthly for all the clients
reported: Nearly 100k monthly emails, $45k MRR, $3k–$6k packages, at least 16 hours/day and substantial expenses.
calculation: No profit calculation supported.
limits: Revenue and sending scale do not establish sustainability; strongest use is capacity caution, not a target operating model.

anchor: 8+ years agency owner. 600+ clients. AMA
reported: Eight-plus years, work with 600-plus clients, multiple-six-figure business.
calculation: No current active-client, retention, close-rate or profit calculation supported.
limits: Historical experience claim; not verified firm size or evidence supporting every recommendation in the AMA.

anchor: Lets say you spend $1500/m
reported: $1,500 ad spend / $60 calls = 25 calls; assume 20% close = five customers; $1,500/customer = $7,500 value.
calculation: $300 ad-only CAC at those assumptions; five times ad spend in billed value before delivery and other costs.
limits: Not an observed result or guaranteed ROAS. Attendance, qualification, collection, tax, margin, labor and retention are absent.

anchor: I was able to book probably 10 meetings in my first 3 months
reported: 100 dials/day, roughly ten meetings and first client in three months; later 30-day free management followed by proposed full-price month two.
calculation: Cannot compute meeting rate without actual calling days, completed dials and duplicate-contact counts.
limits: 5k offer currency not specified. Client pays ad spend. First-client churn sentence and exact closing improvement are incomplete.

anchor: hosting and maintenance retainers up to about $140k per year
reported: Around $140k/year hosting/maintenance, hosting for 200, 30 maintenance plans, five large referrers, roughly ten builds last month.
calculation: $140k/12 ≈ $11,667 monthly equivalent; not verified monthly recurring revenue.
limits: Currency code and gross/net basis unclear. Hosting and maintenance customers can overlap. Same operator as T05; do not double-count corroboration.

anchor: Sent 600+ cold DMs on Instagram.
reported: 600-plus DMs over two months, ten-plus styles, multiple offer labels, no repeatable acquisition process.
calculation: No reply or close rate calculable.
limits: Do not turn 'struggling' into an invented exact zero-client count. Repeated copy changes confound the learning.

anchor: I book calls for less than $100 each and have a 95% show up rate.
reported: Under $100 per booked call and 95% attendance in an unspecified different niche.
calculation: No customer CAC without close rate.
limits: Not MedSpa data; no sample, geography or channel cost boundary. Separate from another commenter's undefined 20% CR.

anchor: cold called and emailed at least 50 of them. Out of those 50, 14
reported: At least 50 businesses approached, 14 agreed, nine paid.
calculation: Using 50 exactly would give 28% agreed and 18% paid; these are upper bounds if actual contacts exceed 50. 9/14 = 64.29% agreement-to-paid if nested.
limits: Mixed email/calling; no timeframe, pricing or invoices. Tool promotion and the 'at least' qualifier matter.

anchor: generated almost €11k in order volume
reported: Five clients over three months; nearly €11k order volume; first two heavily discounted/effectively free; first three from Reddit/network, next two cold email.
calculation: No cold-email rate because send count is missing.
limits: Order value is not cash received or profit. Existing sales experience and network reduce comparability with a zero-experience founder.

anchor: 150 personalized emails in the last 2 months but got only 2 replies and 0 clients
reported: 150 personalized emails, two replies, zero clients, two months.
calculation: 2/150 = 1.33% total replies; observed sends-to-client = 0% for this cohort.
limits: Personalization alone is not proof of good targeting or deliverability; no information about proof, offer or positive reply quality.

anchor: Expect 2-8% reply rate if your targeting is honest.
reported: Claims three retainer clients; prescribes 300 qualified leads, 25 daily sends, 2–8% reply rate, two to three hours/day, four to eight weeks before first payment.
calculation: With an explicitly assumed five-day week: 125 sends × 2–8% = 2.5–10 total replies/week. Qualified conversations are a separate measure.
limits: No empirical denominator connects the three clients to those rates. The claim of roughly one weekly conversation cannot be derived without qualification assumptions.

anchor: Day 14: breakup
reported: Touches at days 0, 3, 7 and 14; paid fixed-fee pilot; ask each paying client for two introductions.
calculation: Four touches are messages, not four unique prospects.
limits: Disagrees with T04. No sequence-level marginal response data; introductions are an ask, not an expected yield.

anchor: 1%+ replies and 0.5%+
reported: 1%+ replies and 0.5%+ interested replies characterized as good cold-email benchmarks.
calculation: Keep total and interested replies as separate rates on a defined cohort; no derived conversion rate is warranted.
limits: No industry, geography, list, sample or denominator definition. Different from the same author's 3–5% statement in T01.

anchor: Les recos représentent environ 60 % de nos signatures.
reported: About 60% of signatures from referrals; two or three partner relationships; two to three months to start partnerships; 12–18 months for content; three to five monthly inbound leads; sales cycle reportedly half as long.
calculation: No total-client or CAC calculation without volumes and costs.
limits: Small SEO agency in France. Stopped cold email and Sales Navigator after six months. Translation is a paraphrase; time ranges are not universal.

anchor: CAC for SEO is like $250-$500 depending on the niche.
reported: SEO/reputation Meta CAC $250–$500; web-design Google CAC about $500 at $5,000 average ticket; $50–$200 daily spend; US/Canada excluding California; instant forms.
calculation: $500 / $5,000 = 10% ad spend relative to average ticket; not gross margin or fully loaded CAC.
limits: Currency code not explicit. No cohort period, independent evidence, show rate or full attribution model. Not an India forecast.

anchor: My income was tied to 3-4 people
reported: Most income dependent on three or four contacts; restricted public attribution of prior work.
calculation: No concentration percentage or revenue total supplied.
limits: Contacts are not necessarily distinct paying accounts. Another commenter's four-client base is a separate account.

anchor: It accounts for about 80% of my new clients.
reported: About 80% of new clients from hyperlocal relationship-based networking after a couple of years.
calculation: No count or CAC calculable.
limits: No sample, industry or window. Relationship building is not an instant cash-flow intervention.

anchor: 100 targeted outreaches give you
reported: 60–90 day channel focus; example 100 contacts → ten conversations → two clients.
calculation: Example implies 10% contact-to-conversation, 20% conversation-to-close and 2% contact-to-close.
limits: Hypothetical illustration; not an observed result. The comment also promotes a tool built around the process.

anchor: CAC is like $250-$400 ish. Any niche.
reported: Facebook client acquisition cost around $250–$400, framed as any niche.
calculation: No valid unit-economics forecast without ticket, margin, retention and cost boundary.
limits: Broad extrapolation without evidence; later T21 discussion provides narrower offer/geography conditions and different ranges from the same author.

anchor: hvac firm with just 125 emails lol.
reported: First HVAC client from 125 emails, while age 17.
calculation: 1/125 = 0.8% sends-to-client if the cohort is complete and attribution direct.
limits: One win; missing reply counts, message sequence, revenue, delivery and recipient details. Not a repeatable expected yield.
